headline: RIO TINTO CEO WARNS OF HISTORIC COPPER DEFICIT AT APEC — Urges Government Cooperation on 40% Lithium Shortfall by 2035
snippet: Rio Tinto CEO Simon Trott used the APEC summit stage in Shenzhen on November 18 to deliver a stark message: without closer collaboration between mining companies and governments, the world faces a 30% copper deficit and 40% lithium shortfall by 2035, according to IEA projections. Trott's comments, delivered as Rio posted 646,000 tonnes of copper output in the first nine months of 2026 (up 1% year-on-year), underscore that even the world's largest miners cannot bridge the supply gap alone — a backdrop that strengthens the long-term investment case for junior copper and lithium developers even as near-term prices face macro headwinds.

headline: SQM Q3 2026 BEAT: LITHIUM PROFIT RISES 36% YoY WITH RECORD VOLUMES — Recovery Signals China Demand Floor Is Holding
snippet: Chile's SQM (NYSE: SQM) reported Q3 2026 net profit up approximately 36% year-over-year with record lithium sales volumes, beating Wall Street expectations and confirming that the lithium price recovery emerging in mid-2026 is translating into earnings. The result, released after the November 17 close, marks the first clean read on whether structural supply discipline is beginning to bite into China's demand appetite — and arrives as a rare positive data point for battery metals investors enduring simultaneous pressure from AI demand repricing and hawkish Fed policy this week.

headline: GOLD SETTLES AT $3,765 — Full-Day Loss Confirms 14-Month Low; $3,700 Now the Last Line Before Long-Term Trend Break
snippet: Gold settled near $3,765 per ounce on November 18 — completing a full-day decline of approximately 2.1% and confirming the second consecutive session at 14-month lows. Multiple data points through the afternoon (Fortune at $3,786 at 8:55 a.m. ET, World Forex Rates at $3,764.75 at 12:31 p.m. GMT) place the close below $3,780, with the cumulative decline from October's post-FOMC minutes high now approaching $200. With no major catalyst before the December 9 FOMC decision, analysts identify $3,700 as the last meaningful technical support before gold enters price territory not seen since mid-2025.

headline: GLOBAL LITHIUM SCHEME BOOKLET FILED WITH ASIC — Titan's A$333M Cash Bid at A$1.15/Share Moves to December Shareholder Vote
snippet: Global Lithium Resources (ASX: GL1) confirmed the registration of its scheme booklet with ASIC on November 18, clearing the way for the document to be dispatched to shareholders by November 23 ahead of a December scheme meeting. UAE-backed Titan Australia Mining's A$333 million all-cash bid at A$1.15 per share represents a 73% premium to GL1's pre-announcement price; the deal still requires FIRB and ACCC approval, with implementation targeted for mid-January 2027. For lithium M&A watchers, the booklet filing is the final procedural milestone before shareholders vote on a deal that benchmarks valuation for ASX hard-rock lithium developers at a time of ongoing price weakness.

headline: PHOENIX METALS HITS 169m AT 1.30% CuEq IN FIRST LEXINGTON HOLE — Every Hole Intersects; BC Copper-Gold System Confirms Bulk-Tonnage Scale
snippet: Phoenix Metals (TSX: PCA) reported its first drill results from the Lexington copper-gold target in BC's Greenwood district on November 18, with a lead intercept of 169 metres at 1.30% copper-equivalent (1.02 g/t Au, 0.22% Cu, 3.8 g/t Ag) and every hole in the nine-hole program intersecting mineralization. The Lexington target sits 15 km south of the historic Phoenix Cu-Au pit and was designed to test for near-surface bulk-tonnage porphyry-style mineralization. A 100% hit rate from first-pass drilling with widths over 100 metres is statistically unusual, suggesting the system has the size needed to support an economic resource even at modest grades — a meaningful signal in a district where few early-stage programs deliver results this broad.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING EXTENDS APOLLO 60m BEYOND RESOURCE BOUNDARY — Shallow Halo Hits 146m at 1.07 g/t AuEq in Colombia
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX/NYSE: CNL) reported that drilling at Apollo's shallow halo zone at the Guayabales project in Caldas, Colombia, returned 146.10 metres at 1.07 g/t gold-equivalent — with the intersection extending approximately 60 metres beyond the current mineral resource boundary. The result demonstrates that the Apollo breccia system remains open in multiple directions outside its defined resource shell, adding resource-replacement optionality to one of the most actively drilled gold-copper systems in Latin America. CNL's 13-rig, 90,000-metre 2026 program targets a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate in 2027.

headline: VISCOUNT MINING IDENTIFIES 3 NEAR-SURFACE PORPHYRY TARGETS AT PASSIFLORA — Above 843m Mineralized Interval; Drone Survey Confirms District Scale
snippet: Viscount Mining (TSX-V: VML) has identified three near-surface gold-copper porphyry targets at its Passiflora area at the Silver Cliff project in Colorado, all within roughly 500 metres of surface above a previously reported 843.9-metre mineralized intercept. A high-resolution Rosor drone survey confirmed the targets are part of a district-scale system; the significance for investors is that near-surface porphyry targets sitting above a known deep intercept of that length suggest the mineralizing system has enough vertical range to support both a shallow open-pit conceptual scenario and a deeper bulk-tonnage resource — a combination that typically attracts both exploration and development interest.

headline: ERIC SPROTT EXERCISES $1.38M IN WARRANTS AT METALSOURCE MINING — Signals Continued Conviction in Silver Hill Gold-Silver in Bear Market
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) received $1.38 million via warrant exercises by Eric Sprott at its Silver Hill gold-silver exploration project — a signal that the veteran precious metals investor is maintaining his position in the company despite the ongoing gold and silver bear market. For retail investors tracking smart-money activity, Sprott warrant exercises at junior explorers have historically served as a conviction indicator: an investor of his caliber exercises (rather than letting expire) only when their underlying view on the asset remains intact. The capital will advance Silver Hill's exploration program.

headline: THISTLE RESOURCES OPTIONS 100% OF LITTLE RIVER GOLD IN NEW BRUNSWICK'S BATHURST CAMP — Enters Historic Zinc-Gold District
snippet: Thistle Resources (TSX-V: TRCG) signed an option agreement on November 18 to acquire 100% of the Little River Gold Project in New Brunswick's Bathurst Mining Camp — the same prolific polymetallic belt that hosted the Brunswick zinc mine, one of the world's largest zinc operations before it closed in 2013. The acquisition adds an early-stage gold target in a structurally significant district that has seen renewed junior exploration interest as operators seek underexplored gold systems adjacent to historically mined base metals corridors. No drill results are yet available; the significance is the district entry at a moment when NB exploration permits are flowing and infrastructure costs remain lower than western Canadian alternatives.
